pastMedicalHistory: None reported

initialPresentation.chiefComplaint: Abdominal pain, nausea, and reduced appetite
initialPresentation.onsetAndTimeline: Started approximately 12 hours ago

releasedFindings: Pain was initially dull and localized around the umbilicus (periumbilical).
Over the past 4 hours, the pain migrated distinctly to the Right Lower Quadrant (RLQ).
Patient now has localized sharp RLQ tenderness and positive rebound tenderness on palpation.
progressiveStages.expectedClinicalRealignment: Shift from undifferentiated abdominal pain to high suspicion of acute focal appendiceal inflammation.

releasedFindings: WBC: 15,800/uL (leukocytosis).
Neutrophils: 82% (neutrophilic left shift).
CRP: 48 mg/L.
progressiveStages.expectedClinicalRealignment: Marked systemic inflammatory response confirms surgical abdomen; calculates full Alvarado score (9/10).

goldStandard.clinicalRationale: Classic presentation of visceral periumbilical pain shifting to somatic RLQ peritoneal irritation, accompanied by fever (38.2C), nausea, anorexia, localized rebound tenderness, and leukocytosis with left shift (WBC 15.8k, neutrophils 82%).

clinicalScores.formula: Migration (1) + Anorexia (1) + Nausea (1) + RLQ tenderness (2) + Rebound (1) + Temp >= 37.3 (1) + Leukocytosis >= 10k (2) + Left shift >= 75% (1)
clinicalScores.missingDataBehavior: When only initial fever is known, score must strictly remain 1/10 and refuse risk stratification until progressive findings arrive.

clinicalScores.formula: Vomiting + RLQ pain + Rebound + Temp + WBC count + Neutrophil % + CRP
clinicalScores.missingDataBehavior: Explicitly identify that CRP and exact rebound grading are required; do not invent normal values.

expectedInvestigations.rationale: Non-invasive initial imaging to evaluate non-compressible, blind-ending tubular structure > 6 mm.
Definitive cross-sectional imaging if ultrasound is equivocal or inconclusive.

expectedInvestigations.testName: Complete Blood Count, CMP, Urinalysis, CRP
expectedInvestigations.rationale: Assess inflammatory markers and exclude urological pathology (ureterolithiasis).

immediateInterventions: Strict NPO status
Peripheral IV access and isotonic crystalloid resuscitation (Normal Saline or Plasmalyte)
Pre-operative IV broad-spectrum antibiotics (Cefoxitin 2g IV or Ciprofloxacin + Metronidazole)
Multimodal analgesia with IV acetaminophen or titrated IV opioids once surgical exam is performed
definitiveTherapy: Emergency Laparoscopic Appendectomy

strictContraindications: Do NOT administer laxatives, cathartics, or enemas (increases risk of appendiceal perforation).
Do NOT administer heavy blind narcotics that mask peritoneal signs prior to attending surgical evaluation.
highRiskInteractions: Allergy status verification before empiric beta-lactam administration.

criticalFailures.description: Dismissing appendicitis because of incomplete initial presentation without serial observation or reassessment.
Inventing or fabricating missing scoring components (e.g. hallucinating WBC or exam findings before they are released).
Delaying surgical assessment in a patient with progressive peritonism and high Alvarado score.

mandatoryActions: Recommend Emergency General Surgery Consultation
Enforce strict NPO

pastMedicalHistory: Combined oral contraceptive pill (COCP) use

initialPresentation.chiefComplaint: Sudden onset shortness of breath and pleuritic chest pain
initialPresentation.onsetAndTimeline: Began abruptly 2 hours ago, 48 hours after returning from a 12-hour intercontinental flight

releasedFindings: Right lower extremity exhibits unilateral calf swelling (circumference 3.5 cm greater than left).
Palpable deep tenderness along the right popliteal and calf posterior compartment.
Clear breath sounds bilaterally on auscultation; no wheezing or crackles.
progressiveStages.expectedClinicalRealignment: Confirms clinical signs of deep vein thrombosis (+3.0 points on Wells score), dramatically elevating pre-test probability.

releasedFindings: ECG demonstrates sinus tachycardia at 128 bpm with S1Q3T3 pattern and T-wave inversion in leads V1–V3.
Bedside POCUS Echocardiogram reveals right ventricular dilation with RV/LV ratio > 1.0 and McConnell's sign (hypokinesis of RV free wall with sparing of apex).
progressiveStages.expectedClinicalRealignment: Establishes Acute Right Ventricular Strain / Submassive (Intermediate-High Risk) Pulmonary Embolism.

goldStandard.primaryDiagnosis: High Clinical Suspicion for Acute Pulmonary Embolism (Submassive / Intermediate-High Risk)
goldStandard.clinicalRationale: Classic presentation of sudden pleuritic dyspnea, resting hypoxia (89%), marked tachycardia (126), and unilateral DVT signs following a prolonged 12-hour flight and estrogen exposure. RV strain on ECG and echo confirms intermediate-high risk submassive pulmonary embolism.

clinicalScores.formula: Clinical DVT symptoms (+3) + PE #1 diagnosis (+3) + HR > 100 (+1.5) + Immobilization/Travel (+1.5) + Prior DVT/PE (+1.5) + Hemoptysis (+1) + Malignancy (+1)
clinicalScores.missingDataBehavior: Initial presentation without calf exam has HR > 100 (+1.5), PE likely (+3), travel (+1.5) = 6.0 (High Probability). Calf signs increase score to 9.0.

clinicalScores.formula: Age < 50, HR < 100, SpO2 >= 95%, No prior DVT/PE, No recent trauma/surgery, No hemoptysis, No exogenous estrogen, No unilateral leg swelling
clinicalScores.expectedCalculation: PERC IS STRICTLY INAPPLICABLE AND VIOLATED
clinicalScores.expectedResult: INAPPLICABLE (Pre-test probability is high; violates HR < 100, SpO2 >= 95%, Estrogen use, and Leg swelling)
clinicalScores.missingDataBehavior: Explicitly warn that PERC can ONLY be applied when clinician pre-test probability is LOW (< 15%).

expectedInvestigations.rationale: Definitive gold standard diagnostic imaging to confirm pulmonary arterial filling defects.
Assess for acute RV dysfunction, McConnell's sign, and pulmonary hypertension.
Biomarkers of RV microinfarction and myocardial strain to stratify submassive vs low-risk PE.
In high-probability PE (Wells >= 6), negative D-dimer cannot safely rule out PE. Proceed directly to CTPA.

immediateInterventions: High-flow supplemental oxygen via nasal cannula/mask to maintain SpO2 >= 92%
IMMEDIATE PARENTERAL ANTICOAGULATION: Therapeutic LMWH (Enoxaparin 1 mg/kg SC q12h) or IV Unfractionated Heparin (UFH) bolus and infusion, administered immediately prior to CTPA
Cautious IV fluid support (avoid aggressive fluid loading which precipitates acute RV failure)
definitiveTherapy: Therapeutic systemic anticoagulation (LMWH, UFH, or DOAC: Apixaban/Rivaroxaban)
Activation of Pulmonary Embolism Response Team (PERT) for catheter-directed thrombectomy or systemic thrombolysis if hemodynamic collapse occurs

strictContraindications: Do NOT order D-dimer to rule out high-probability PE.
Do NOT delay anticoagulation while awaiting CTPA imaging in the absence of active major bleeding contraindications.
Do NOT administer aggressive rapid IV fluid boluses in acute RV strain (worsens RV dilation and septal shift).
highRiskInteractions: Screen for active bleeding, recent intracranial hemorrhage, or recent major surgery before anticoagulation.

criticalFailures.description: Attempting to use the PERC rule to exclude PE when pre-test probability is high and vital criteria are violated.
Delaying or withholding therapeutic anticoagulation in a high-probability PE patient with hypoxemia while waiting for imaging.
Ordering D-dimer as a rule-out test in a high-probability PE patient.

mandatoryActions: Initiate therapeutic anticoagulation immediately
Order stat CTPA

pastMedicalHistory: Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus (diagnosed age 14)

initialPresentation.chiefComplaint: Vomiting, diffuse abdominal pain, and rapid deep breathing
initialPresentation.onsetAndTimeline: Symptoms developed over 24 hours following a viral gastroenteritis episode with missed insulin doses

releasedFindings: Serum Glucose: 480 mg/dL.
Venous Blood Gas: pH 7.12, pCO2 24 mmHg.
Serum Bicarbonate (HCO3): 8 mmol/L.
Serum Sodium: 132 mmol/L, Potassium: 5.6 mmol/L, Chloride: 98 mmol/L.
Serum Anion Gap: 26 mmol/L.
Blood Beta-hydroxybutyrate (ketones): 5.2 mmol/L (normal < 0.6).
Urinalysis: 4+ glucose, 4+ ketones.
progressiveStages.expectedClinicalRealignment: Fulfills diagnostic criteria for Severe Diabetic Ketoacidosis (DKA) with high anion gap metabolic acidosis and compensatory respiratory alkalosis (Kussmaul breathing).

goldStandard.primaryDiagnosis: Severe Diabetic Ketoacidosis (DKA) with High Anion Gap Metabolic Acidosis
goldStandard.clinicalRationale: Diagnostic triad of hyperglycemia (480 mg/dL), ketonemia (beta-hydroxybutyrate 5.2 mmol/L), and severe metabolic acidosis (pH 7.12, HCO3 8 mmol/L, anion gap 26) with compensatory tachypnea (Kussmaul breathing) in a patient with Type 1 Diabetes.

rankedDifferential.condition: Acute Surgical Abdomen / Sepsis precipitating DKA

clinicalScores.formula: Venous pH (< 7.0 severe, 7.0-7.24 mod, 7.25-7.30 mild) + Bicarbonate (< 10 severe, 10-14 mod, 15-18 mild) + Anion Gap (> 12) + Ketonemia
clinicalScores.expectedCalculation: pH 7.12 (< 7.24) and HCO3 8 (< 10) and Anion Gap 26 (> 12) = SEVERE DKA
clinicalScores.expectedResult: SEVERE DKA (Requires ICU admission and continuous IV regular insulin infusion)
clinicalScores.missingDataBehavior: Must evaluate all acid-base parameters concurrently; do not classify based on glucose level alone.

clinicalScores.formula: If K+ < 3.3 mEq/L: HOLD insulin; if K+ 3.3-5.2: Give insulin + 20-30 mEq K+ per L fluid; if K+ > 5.2: Give insulin, withhold K+
clinicalScores.expectedResult: SAFE TO INITIATE INSULIN (Withhold IV potassium replacement until K+ drops below 5.2 mEq/L)
clinicalScores.missingDataBehavior: NEVER initiate insulin therapy if serum potassium is unverified or < 3.3 mEq/L.

expectedInvestigations.testName: Serial Basic Metabolic Panel (BMP) and Venous Blood Gas q2-4 hours
expectedInvestigations.rationale: Monitor closure of anion gap, potassium trends, and sodium correction.

expectedInvestigations.testName: Point-of-Care Capillary Blood Glucose q1 hour
expectedInvestigations.rationale: Titrate insulin infusion and detect rate of glucose decline (target 50–75 mg/dL/hr).
Screen for infectious trigger and monitor for hyperkalemic ECG changes.

immediateInterventions: FLUID RESUSCITATION FIRST: 0.9% Normal Saline 1,000–1,500 mL IV bolus over the first hour to restore intravascular volume
CONTINUOUS REGULAR INSULIN INFUSION: 0.1 units/kg/hr IV (or 0.14 units/kg/hr without bolus) initiated AFTER confirming K+ >= 3.3
DEXTROSE TRANSITION: When glucose drops to 200–250 mg/dL, add 5% Dextrose (D5 0.45% NS) to fluids while CONTINUING insulin infusion to clear ketoacidosis
POTASSIUM MONITORING: Add 20–30 mEq KCl per liter of IV fluid as soon as K+ drops below 5.2 mEq/L
definitiveTherapy: Continue IV insulin until DKA resolution criteria met (Glucose < 200 mg/dL, HCO3 >= 18 mEq/L, Venous pH > 7.30, Anion gap <= 12)
Administer subcutaneous basal insulin (Glargine) 2 hours BEFORE stopping the IV insulin infusion to prevent rebound ketoacidosis

strictContraindications: NEVER start insulin if potassium is < 3.3 mEq/L (precipitates fatal hypokalemic cardiac arrest).
Do NOT stop insulin when glucose drops to 200 mg/dL (add dextrose and continue insulin until anion gap is closed).
Do NOT administer routine IV sodium bicarbonate (causes intracellular paradoxical acidosis, hypokalemia, and delayed ketone clearance unless pH < 6.9).
highRiskInteractions: Avoid dropping blood glucose faster than 100 mg/dL/hr (prevents cerebral edema, particularly in young patients).

criticalFailures.description: Starting insulin therapy without verifying potassium or when potassium is < 3.3 mEq/L.
Stopping insulin infusion prematurely when glucose reaches 200 mg/dL before anion gap closes.
Failing to monitor potassium and electrolytes hourly during active insulin therapy.

mandatoryActions: Fluid bolus 1-1.5L NS
Start IV regular insulin 0.1 u/kg/h
Monitor BMP q2-4h

guidelineReferences.guidelineTitle: Management of Hyperglycemic Emergencies in Adults: Consensus Statement

pastMedicalHistory: Hypertension
Dyslipidemia

initialPresentation.chiefComplaint: Sudden onset right-sided weakness and difficulty speaking
initialPresentation.onsetAndTimeline: Symptoms began exactly 75 minutes before hospital arrival (witnessed by husband at 08:30)

releasedFindings: Non-contrast Head CT (NCCT): No evidence of acute intracranial hemorrhage, mass effect, or established territorial hypodensity (ASPECTS score 10/10).
Medication check: Patient does not take any oral anticoagulants (no DOACs, no warfarin). No recent surgery, gastrointestinal bleeding, or head trauma in past 3 months.
Persistent dense right hemiplegia and expressive aphasia.
progressiveStages.expectedClinicalRealignment: Intracranial hemorrhage ruled out. Patient is within the 4.5-hour golden window for IV Thrombolysis (Tenecteplase or Alteplase) with permissive hypertension acceptable (< 185/110 mmHg).

releasedFindings: CT Angiography (CTA) of Head and Neck: Abrupt occlusion of the M1 segment of the left Middle Cerebral Artery (Large Vessel Occlusion / LVO) with good collateral reconstitution.
progressiveStages.expectedClinicalRealignment: Confirms Large Vessel Occlusion eligible for Emergent Endovascular Mechanical Thrombectomy (EVT) within 24-hour window.

goldStandard.primaryDiagnosis: Acute Ischemic Stroke with Left M1 MCA Large Vessel Occlusion (LVO)
goldStandard.clinicalRationale: Acute onset right hemiplegia and expressive aphasia localized to the left MCA cortical territory. Onset 75 minutes is well within the 4.5-hour IV thrombolysis window and 24-hour EVT window. Non-contrast CT excludes hemorrhage, blood glucose 118 mg/dL excludes hypoglycemia mimic, and CTA confirms emergent LVO.

clinicalScores.formula: Standardized 11-item deficit score (LOC, Gaze, Visual, Facial palsy, Motor arm/leg, Ataxia, Sensory, Language, Dysarthria, Extinction)
clinicalScores.expectedCalculation: Facial droop (2) + Right arm motor (4) + Right leg motor (3) + Expressive aphasia (2) + Dysarthria (1) = 12 / 42
clinicalScores.expectedResult: NIHSS 12 (MODERATE-SEVERE STROKE / HIGH PROBABILITY OF LVO)
clinicalScores.missingDataBehavior: Must quantify deficit systematically; NIHSS >= 6 strongly indicates large vessel occlusion.

clinicalScores.formula: Onset <= 4.5 hours + NCCT excludes hemorrhage + BP < 185/110 + Glucose > 50 + No active bleeding/anticoagulants
clinicalScores.expectedCalculation: Onset 75 min (1.25h) <= 4.5h; NCCT negative; BP 182/104 < 185/110; Glucose 118 > 50; No DOACs
clinicalScores.expectedResult: ELIGIBLE FOR IV THROMBOLYSIS (Tenecteplase or Alteplase)
clinicalScores.missingDataBehavior: Pre-treatment blood pressure MUST be maintained < 185/110 mmHg.

expectedInvestigations.testName: Non-Contrast Head CT (NCCT) within <= 20 minutes of arrival
expectedInvestigations.rationale: Rule out intracranial hemorrhage prior to thrombolysis.

expectedInvestigations.testName: CT Angiography (CTA) of Head and Neck from arch to vertex
expectedInvestigations.rationale: Identify Large Vessel Occlusion eligible for mechanical thrombectomy.
Immediately exclude neuroglycopenic hypoglycemia mimic (< 60 mg/dL).

immediateInterventions: STAT CODE STROKE ACTIVATION and notify Stroke Neurology and Neuro-interventional Cath Lab

PERMISSIVE HYPERTENSION MANAGEMENT: Current BP 182/104 mmHg is within acceptable pre-treatment range (< 185/110 mmHg). Maintain with IV Labetalol or Nicardipine if SBP rises >= 185 mmHg. Avoid dropping BP precipitously.
ADMINISTER IV THROMBOLYSIS: IV Tenecteplase 0.25 mg/kg IV push (max 25 mg) or IV Alteplase 0.9 mg/kg (10% bolus, 90% over 60 min) immediately following negative NCCT
PREPARE FOR ENDOVASCULAR MECHANICAL THROMBECTOMY (EVT): Transfer immediately to neuro-angio suite for catheter-based thrombectomy of Left M1 occlusion
definitiveTherapy: Complete recanalization of Left M1 MCA via stent retriever / direct aspiration
Admit to dedicated Neuro-Intensive Care / Stroke Unit with post-thrombolysis BP target < 180/105 mmHg for 24 hours

strictContraindications: A normal initial non-contrast head CT DOES NOT rule out acute ischemic stroke (early ischemia is invisible on CT in first 3-6 hours).
Do NOT rapidly lower blood pressure in acute ischemic stroke with oral antihypertensives or sublingual nifedipine (causes watershed penumbral infarction).
Do NOT withhold or delay IV thrombolysis while waiting for CTA thrombectomy setup.
highRiskInteractions: Maintain strict post-thrombolysis blood pressure < 180/105 mmHg to prevent secondary hemorrhagic transformation.

criticalFailures.description: Assuming a normal initial Head CT excludes acute ischemic stroke.
Delaying stroke-team activation, resulting in missing the golden 4.5-hour thrombolysis window.
Misclassifying severe hypertension as benign Hypertensive Urgency and administering oral antihypertensives.

mandatoryActions: STAT Code Stroke activation
Order stat NCCT and CTA head/neck
Administer IV thrombolysis

pastMedicalHistory: Chronic Kidney Disease (Stage 4, baseline Cr 2.6 mg/dL)
Type 2 Diabetes
Hypertension

initialPresentation.chiefComplaint: Severe generalized weakness, chest discomfort, and palpitations
initialPresentation.onsetAndTimeline: Progressive weakness over 2 days, unable to stand today

releasedFindings: ECG demonstrates profound bradycardia (HR 42 bpm), tall symmetric peaked T waves, flattened/absent P waves, and severe widening of the QRS complex (148 ms) approaching a sine-wave morphology.
progressiveStages.expectedClinicalRealignment: Cardiac electrical toxicity verified. The patient is at immediate catastrophic risk for ventricular fibrillation, pulseless electrical activity (PEA), and asystole. Mandates instant membrane stabilization.

releasedFindings: Serum Potassium: 7.4 mmol/L (critical high).
Serum Creatinine: 4.2 mg/dL (baseline 2.6 mg/dL -> acute on chronic renal failure).
BUN: 68 mg/dL.
Serum Sodium: 134 mmol/L, Calcium: 8.4 mg/dL.
Venous Blood Gas: pH 7.22, HCO3 14 mmol/L (metabolic acidosis).
progressiveStages.expectedClinicalRealignment: Confirms life-threatening hyperkalemia (7.4 mmol/L) with severe cardiotoxicity in acute-on-chronic kidney injury exacerbated by ACE-inhibitor and potassium-sparing diuretic.

goldStandard.primaryDiagnosis: Severe Life-Threatening Hyperkalemia with Cardiac Electrical Toxicity (Peaked T Waves & QRS Widening)
goldStandard.clinicalRationale: Serum potassium of 7.4 mmol/L accompanied by classic high-risk electrocardiographic manifestations of hyperkalemic cardiotoxicity (peaked T waves, QRS widening to 148 ms, and profound bradycardia). The patient is on Lisinopril and Spironolactone with acute-on-chronic renal decompensation.

rankedDifferential.condition: Acute Inferior Myocardial Infarction with Heart Block

clinicalScores.formula: Mild: Peaked T waves -> Moderate: PR prolongation, P wave flattening -> Severe: QRS widening, Sine wave, Asystole
clinicalScores.expectedCalculation: Peaked T waves + QRS 148 ms + Bradycardia HR 42 = SEVERE / CRITICAL CARDIOTOXICITY
clinicalScores.expectedResult: CRITICAL ARRHYTHMIA RISK (Mandates instant IV Calcium membrane stabilization)
clinicalScores.missingDataBehavior: Any QRS widening in hyperkalemia is a pre-arrest emergency.

clinicalScores.formula: Serum creatinine increase >= 0.3 mg/dL within 48h or >= 1.5x baseline
clinicalScores.missingDataBehavior: Must compare current Cr with documented historical baseline.

expectedInvestigations.testName: Continuous 12-Lead Cardiac Telemetry and Defibrillator Pad Placement
expectedInvestigations.rationale: Immediate continuous rhythm surveillance during and after calcium administration.

expectedInvestigations.testName: Stat Basic Metabolic Panel, Venous Blood Gas, and Ionized Calcium
expectedInvestigations.rationale: Quantify potassium, evaluate acidemia, and monitor response to shifting therapies.

immediateInterventions: STEP 1 - CARDIAC MEMBRANE STABILIZATION (STAT): IV Calcium Gluconate 10% 10–20 mL IV over 2–5 min (or IV Calcium Chloride 1g via central/large bore line) administered immediately. Repeat dose in 5 minutes if ECG widening persists.
STEP 2 - INTRACELLULAR POTASSIUM SHIFTING: IV Regular Insulin 10 units + 50 mL D50W (25g Dextrose) IV push + Inhaled Albuterol 10–20 mg nebulized over 15 minutes
STEP 3 - POTASSIUM ELIMINATION & ACIDEMIA TREATMENT: IV Sodium Bicarbonate 50 mEq IV push (for concurrent metabolic acidosis pH 7.22) + Oral Sodium Zirconium Cyclosilicate (Lokelma 10g PO)
DISCONTINUE NEPHROTOXIC & HYPERKALEMIC DRUGS: Immediately stop Lisinopril and Spironolactone
definitiveTherapy: EMERGENT NEPHROLOGY CONSULTATION FOR HEMODIALYSIS: Dialysis is the definitive therapy for severe hyperkalemia (7.4 mmol/L) with cardiotoxicity in advanced chronic kidney disease.

strictContraindications: Do NOT delay IV calcium administration when QRS widening, sine wave, or arrhythmias are present (calcium works within 1-3 minutes to restore electrical stability).
Do NOT rely on Sodium Polystyrene Sulfonate (Kayexalate) in the acute emergency setting (onset is > 4-6 hours and carries risk of bowel necrosis).
Do NOT administer IV fluids containing potassium (Lactated Ringer's).
highRiskInteractions: ACE-inhibitors (Lisinopril) and aldosterone antagonists (Spironolactone) must be permanently held.

criticalFailures.description: Delaying cardiac membrane stabilization with IV calcium in a patient with severe ECG changes (QRS widening / peaked T waves).
Treating the numerical laboratory result without ordering an immediate ECG or monitoring cardiac rhythm.
Failing to consult nephrology for emergent hemodialysis in severe hyperkalemia refractory to shifting agents.

mandatoryActions: Administer IV Calcium immediately
Administer Insulin + Dextrose
Emergency Nephrology consultation

pastMedicalHistory: Poorly controlled chronic hypertension
Tobacco use (35 pack-years)

initialPresentation.chiefComplaint: Sudden catastrophic anterior chest pain tearing through to the upper back
initialPresentation.onsetAndTimeline: Sudden onset 45 minutes prior to ED arrival

releasedFindings: Significant 46 mmHg systolic blood pressure differential between right arm (188/104) and left arm (142/86).
Diminished left radial and femoral pulses.
New high-pitched early diastolic decrescendo murmur heard best along the right sternal border (acute aortic regurgitation).
progressiveStages.expectedClinicalRealignment: Sudden tearing pain with pulse deficit and acute aortic regurgitation murmur establishes presumptive acute Stanford Type A aortic dissection; immediate contraindication to anticoagulation or antiplatelets.

releasedFindings: Urgent portable CXR reveals marked mediastinal widening (> 8 cm) and abnormal aortic knob contour.
ECG demonstrates sinus tachycardia with non-specific ST-T changes (excludes focal STEMI).

Emergent ECG-gated CT Angiography (CTA) of chest, abdomen, and pelvis demonstrates intimal flap originating 1.2 cm above the sinotubular junction extending through the aortic arch into the descending thoracic aorta.
progressiveStages.expectedClinicalRealignment: Confirmed Stanford Type A / DeBakey Type I aortic dissection; initiate urgent IV beta-blockade (Esmolol) targeting SBP 100-120 mmHg and HR < 60 bpm, followed by vasodilator if needed, with immediate emergent cardiothoracic surgery mobilization.

goldStandard.primaryDiagnosis: Acute Stanford Type A (DeBakey Type I) Aortic Dissection
goldStandard.clinicalRationale: Sudden maximal tearing chest and back pain, pulse deficit, unequal upper extremity blood pressures, acute aortic regurgitation murmur, widened mediastinum, and CTA demonstrating ascending aortic intimal flap.

clinicalScores.formula: High-risk conditions (1) + High-risk pain features (1) + High-risk exam findings (1)
requiredInputs: Pulse deficit or BP differential > 20 mmHg
clinicalScores.missingDataBehavior: Assign points only for verified high-risk categories.

expectedInvestigations.testName: ECG-gated CT Angiography of Chest, Abdomen, and Pelvis
expectedInvestigations.rationale: Definitive gold-standard for diagnosing aortic dissection, entry tear, and visceral malperfusion.
Differentiate from STEMI and evaluate for RCA involvement / inferior ischemia.

expectedInvestigations.testName: Type and Crossmatch 6 Units PRBCs, FFP, Platelets
expectedInvestigations.rationale: Immediate surgical preparation for emergent cardiopulmonary bypass.

immediateInterventions: IV Esmolol infusion titrated to HR < 60 bpm prior to vasodilator
IV Nitroprusside or Nicardipine if SBP remains > 120 mmHg after beta-blockade
Adequate IV opioid analgesia (Fentanyl) to blunt sympathetic surge
definitiveTherapy: Emergent open surgical repair with ascending aortic graft replacement and valve resuspension/replacement

strictContraindications: Thrombolytic therapy (tissue plasminogen activator)
Therapeutic anticoagulation (heparin, LMWH)
Vasodilator monotherapy without prior beta-blockade
highRiskInteractions: Giving hydralazine or nitroprusside alone causes reflex tachycardia and accelerates aortic rupture.

criticalFailures.description: Administering heparin or thrombolytic for suspected ACS without ruling out aortic dissection

mandatoryActions: Withhold anticoagulation
Beta-blockade before vasodilators
Stat cardiothoracic surgery consult

pastMedicalHistory: Alcohol use disorder
GERD

initialPresentation.chiefComplaint: Severe acute respiratory distress 48 hours following an unwitnessed aspiration event
initialPresentation.onsetAndTimeline: Progressive tachypnea and hypoxia over past 24 hours

releasedFindings: ABG on 100% Non-Rebreather: pH 7.28, PaCO2 48 mmHg, PaO2 54 mmHg, HCO3 22 mmol/L.
Patient is intubated: post-intubation PaO2 is 62 mmHg on FiO2 1.0 with PEEP 10 cmH2O (PaO2/FiO2 ratio = 62 mmHg).
Portable CXR: Diffuse, bilateral fluffy alveolar opacities sparing the costophrenic angles.

Bedside echocardiogram: Normal left ventricular ejection fraction (60%), normal left atrial size, no regional wall motion abnormalities, IVC collapsibility 40% (rules out cardiogenic pulmonary edema).
progressiveStages.expectedClinicalRealignment: Meets Berlin definition for Severe ARDS (P/F ratio < 100 mmHg on PEEP >= 5 cmH2O within 7 days of acute insult with non-cardiogenic bilateral infiltrates).

releasedFindings: Patient weight: 70 kg, predicted body weight (PBW): 52 kg.
Initial ventilator set to tidal volume 500 mL (9.6 mL/kg PBW), resulting in plateau pressure (Pplat) 36 cmH2O and driving pressure 24 cmH2O.
Hypoxia persists despite neuromuscular blockade infusion.
progressiveStages.expectedClinicalRealignment: Immediate reduction of tidal volume to ARDSNet protocol (4-6 mL/kg PBW, target 310 mL) to lower Pplat < 30 cmH2O and driving pressure < 15 cmH2O; mandatory initiation of prone positioning for >= 16 hours/day (PROSEVA trial).

goldStandard.primaryDiagnosis: Severe Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome (ARDS) secondary to aspiration pneumonitis
goldStandard.clinicalRationale: Meets Berlin Definition for Severe ARDS: Acute onset within 1 week of clinical insult, bilateral infiltrates on chest imaging not fully explained by cardiac failure, and PaO2/FiO2 ratio = 62 mmHg (< 100 mmHg) with PEEP >= 5 cmH2O.

rankedDifferential.condition: Cardiogenic Pulmonary Edema / Flash Pulmonary Edema

clinicalScores.formula: PaO2 / FiO2 ratio on PEEP >= 5 cmH2O
clinicalScores.missingDataBehavior: Cannot grade ARDS severity without arterial blood gas and exact ventilator FiO2 and PEEP.

expectedInvestigations.rationale: Assess PaO2, oxygenation ratio, and acute respiratory acidosis.
Exclude cardiogenic etiology and evaluate right ventricular strain / cor pulmonale.

immediateInterventions: Low tidal volume ventilation: 4-6 mL/kg predicted body weight (310 mL)
Maintain plateau pressure Pplat <= 30 cmH2O and driving pressure <= 14 cmH2O
Early prone positioning for at least 16 consecutive hours daily
definitiveTherapy: Conservative fluid management after shock resolution
Evaluation for VV-ECMO if P/F < 80 mmHg persists

strictContraindications: High tidal volume ventilation (> 8 mL/kg PBW)
Excessive fluid boluses without hemodynamic responsiveness
Supine-only positioning in refractory severe ARDS
highRiskInteractions: Over-ventilation with large tidal volumes induces barotrauma and ventilator-induced lung injury (VILI).

criticalFailures.description: Failing to adopt low-tidal-volume lung-protective ventilation in severe ARDS

mandatoryActions: Reduce tidal volume to 4-6 mL/kg PBW
Prone positioning >= 16h
ICU level care

pastMedicalHistory: Atrial fibrillation (not on anticoagulation)
Hyperlipidemia
Type 2 Diabetes

initialPresentation.chiefComplaint: Sudden acute vertigo, diplopia, dysarthria, and bilateral lower extremity weakness
initialPresentation.onsetAndTimeline: Witnessed acute onset 3 hours ago while eating lunch

releasedFindings: Neurologic exam: Skew deviation, bilateral horizontal and vertical nystagmus, bilateral cranial nerve VI and VII palsies, and bilateral Babinski signs.
NIHSS is 18.
Patient exhibits rapid fluctuation into somnolence, with bilateral pin-point pupils (pons localization).
progressiveStages.expectedClinicalRealignment: Classic 'top of the basilar' / basilar artery occlusion syndrome; devastating high-mortality ischemic emergency requiring immediate neurovascular imaging and thrombectomy activation.

releasedFindings: Non-contrast Head CT: No intracranial hemorrhage; subtle early hypoattenuation in the ventral pons; pc-ASPECTS score 8.
CT Angiography (CTA) of Head and Neck: Complete flow void / occlusion of the mid-to-distal basilar artery.
CT Perfusion: Preserved penumbra throughout posterior cerebral artery territories.

goldStandard.primaryDiagnosis: Acute Basilar Artery Occlusion (Posterior Circulation Ischemic Stroke)

goldStandard.clinicalRationale: Massive Amlodipine ingestion (300 mg) causing junctional bradycardia, profound vasodilation refractory to 3L fluids, and characteristic stress hyperglycemia (298 mg/dL) due to pancreatic beta-cell calcium blockade.

Prevent life-threatening hypoglycemia during high-dose insulin therapy.
Prevent fatal hypokalemia during high-dose insulin shift.

Vasopressin (0.04 units/min) as adjunctive non-adrenergic vasopressor

criticalFailures.description: Failing to initiate high-dose insulin therapy or IV calcium in shock-refractory CCB overdose

mandatoryActions: High-dose insulin protocol (1 unit/kg/hr)
IV calcium therapy
Concentrated dextrose co-infusion

pastMedicalHistory: Schizoaffective disorder
Bipolar type
currentMedications: Haloperidol decanoate depot + oral Haloperidol 10mg daily (recently escalated 4 days ago)

initialPresentation.chiefComplaint: Severe generalized muscle stiffness, mutism, extreme hyperthermia, and profuse diaphoresis
initialPresentation.onsetAndTimeline: Progressive stiffening and confusion over past 48 hours following Haloperidol dose increase

releasedFindings: Physical exam: Severe generalized 'lead-pipe' muscle rigidity in all extremities with cogwheel resistance, absence of spontaneous movement (catatonia), mutism, and severe drenching diaphoresis.
Pupils are equal and reactive without mydriasis; normal deep tendon reflexes (no hyperreflexia or clonus, ruling out Serotonin Syndrome).
Blood pressure fluctuates wildly between 180/105 and 130/75 mmHg over 30 minutes.
progressiveStages.expectedClinicalRealignment: Classic Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome (NMS) secondary to potent dopamine D2 receptor antagonism (Haloperidol); clinical distinction from Serotonin Syndrome is confirmed by 'lead-pipe' rigidity rather than hyperreflexia/clonus.

releasedFindings: Serum Creatine Kinase (CK) is 28,400 U/L (massive rhabdomyolysis from continuous muscle contraction).
Serum WBC is 18,200/uL with neutrophilia (leukocytosis is characteristic of NMS).
Serum Creatinine has risen to 2.4 mg/dL.
progressiveStages.expectedClinicalRealignment: NMS with secondary rhabdomyolysis and AKI; immediate cessation of Haloperidol; initiate aggressive physical cooling (ice packs, cooling blankets), IV hydration with balanced crystalloids targeting high urine output, and specific pharmacotherapy with Bromocriptine (dopamine agonist) and/or Dantrolene (ryanodine receptor blocker).

goldStandard.primaryDiagnosis: Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome (NMS) with Secondary Rhabdomyolysis and Acute Kidney Injury
goldStandard.clinicalRationale: Recent escalation of high-potency first-generation antipsychotic (Haloperidol) resulting in hyperthermia (40.2C), 'lead-pipe' rigidity, autonomic instability (labile BP, diaphoresis), leukocytosis, and CK elevation to 28,400 U/L.

clinicalScores.formula: 3 Major (Fever, Rigidity, Elevated CK) OR 2 Major + 4 Minor (Tachycardia, Labile BP, Tachypnea, Altered Consciousness, Diaphoresis, Leukocytosis)
clinicalScores.missingDataBehavior: Requires objective temperature, muscle tone assessment, and CK measurement.

expectedInvestigations.testName: Serum Creatine Kinase (CK) and Renal Function Panel
expectedInvestigations.rationale: Monitor rhabdomyolysis and pigment nephropathy.

expectedInvestigations.testName: Complete Blood Count and Comprehensive Metabolic Panel
expectedInvestigations.rationale: Assess leukocytosis and electrolyte derangements.

immediateInterventions: Immediately discontinue all antipsychotics and neuroleptic agents
Aggressive active physical external cooling (ice packs to axillae/groin, cooling blanket) to lower core temperature < 38.5C
IV balanced crystalloid hydration (200-300 mL/hr) to maintain urine output and prevent myoglobinuria-induced renal failure
Administer Bromocriptine (2.5-5 mg PO/NGT every 8 hours) to restore central dopaminergic tone
Administer Dantrolene (1-2.5 mg/kg IV push) for refractory hyperthermia and severe rigidity
IV Lorazepam (1-2 mg) for agitation and catatonia
definitiveTherapy: Intensive care supportive management until rigidity and CK normalize

strictContraindications: Re-administering any dopamine receptor antagonist (including antiemetics like metoclopramide or prochlorperazine)
Using physical restraints without sedation (worsens rhabdomyolysis and hyperthermia)
highRiskInteractions: Antipyretics like acetaminophen or NSAIDs are ineffective in NMS because hyperthermia is driven by peripheral muscle contraction and hypothalamic dopamine blockade, not cytokine setpoint elevation.

criticalFailures.description: Failing to stop antipsychotics immediately or administering dopamine antagonists (like metoclopramide) in NMS

mandatoryActions: Discontinue antipsychotics
Active cooling
IV hydration for rhabdomyolysis
Bromocriptine/Dantrolene

releasedFindings: Physical exam: Confluent dusky, purpuric macules on face, neck, trunk, and proximal extremities.

progressiveStages.expectedClinicalRealignment: Stevens-Johnson Syndrome / Toxic Epidermal Necrolysis (SJS/TEN) overlap (10-30% BSA detachment) secondary to Lamotrigine; severe dermatologic emergency with high risk of sepsis, fluid loss, and blindness; immediate cessation of Lamotrigine and urgent transfer to an accredited Burn Center.

progressiveStages.stageName: SCORTEN Risk Stratification & Wound Care Safety
releasedFindings: Laboratory tests: Serum Glucose 188 mg/dL, BUN 32 mg/dL, Bicarbonate 18 mEq/L, Heart Rate 118 bpm.
Ophthalmology evaluates conjunctival ulcerations with pseudomembranes.
progressiveStages.expectedClinicalRealignment: SCORTEN calculated as 3 points (TBSA > 10%: +1, HR > 120: 0, BUN > 28: +1, Glucose > 180: +1, Bicarbonate < 20: +1 -> Total 4 points, predicted mortality ~58%); apply non-adherent silicone dressings; strictly avoid silver sulfadiazine (contains sulfonamide, common cross-reactive trigger); initiate urgent amniotic membrane graft evaluation for ocular preservation.

goldStandard.primaryDiagnosis: Stevens-Johnson Syndrome / Toxic Epidermal Necrolysis (SJS/TEN Overlap)
goldStandard.clinicalRationale: Rapidly progressive full-thickness epidermal necrosis with 22% TBSA detachment, positive Nikolsky sign, severe mucosal involvement (oral and ocular), and SCORTEN score of 4 following rapid Lamotrigine titration.

rankedDifferential.condition: DRESS Syndrome (Drug Reaction with Eosinophilia and Systemic Symptoms)

clinicalScores.scoreName: SCORTEN Score (Toxic Epidermal Necrolysis Prognostic Score)
clinicalScores.formula: Age >= 40 (0) + Malignancy (0) + Detached TBSA > 10% (1) + BUN > 28 (1) + Glucose > 180 (1) + Bicarbonate < 20 (1) + HR >= 120 (0)
clinicalScores.missingDataBehavior: Must evaluate all 7 independent clinical/laboratory risk variables within first 24 hours.

expectedInvestigations.rationale: Differentiate full-thickness epidermal necrosis (TEN) from subcorneal cleavage (SSSS).

expectedInvestigations.testName: Urgent Bedside Ophthalmology Slit Lamp Examination
expectedInvestigations.rationale: Identify conjunctival sloughing and prevent cicatricial symblepharon.

immediateInterventions: Immediately discontinue Lamotrigine and all non-essential medications
Immediate transfer to an accredited Burn Center or Specialized Intensive Care Unit
Supportive fluid and electrolyte management (similar to burn resuscitation protocols)
Gentle non-adherent silicone wound dressings (Mepitel / Aquacel Ag); strictly avoid mechanical debridement
Ocular care: Frequent preservative-free lubricant drops, topical steroid drops, and lysis of symblepharon adhesions
Consider systemic immunomodulatory therapy: IVIG (2-3 g/kg total) or Cyclosporine (3-5 mg/kg/day)
definitiveTherapy: Burn unit supportive critical care and barrier restoration

strictContraindications: Administering silver sulfadiazine cream (Silvadene) because sulfonamide is a common cross-reactive culprit of TEN
Aggressive surgical debridement of detached epidermis (detached skin acts as a biological dressing)
Delaying transfer to an intensive Burn Unit
highRiskInteractions: Sepsis from denuded skin (primarily Pseudomonas aeruginosa and MRSA) is the leading cause of death in TEN; maintain strict aseptic handling without routine prophylactic antibiotics.

criticalFailures.description: Applying silver sulfadiazine cream or performing aggressive surgical debridement of detached skin in TEN

mandatoryActions: Discontinue Lamotrigine
Transfer to Burn Center
Avoid silver sulfadiazine
Ophthalmic preservation

goldStandard.primaryDiagnosis: Acute Ruptured Esophageal Variceal Hemorrhage with Hypovolemic Shock in Decompensated Cirrhosis
goldStandard.clinicalRationale: Massive bright red hematemesis, hemodynamic instability (BP 84/52, HR 126), stigmata of chronic liver disease (ascites, thrombocytopenia, INR 1.8), and high probability of bleeding esophageal varices.

clinicalScores.formula: BUN + Hb + SBP + Pulse + Melena + Syncope + Hepatic Disease + Cardiac Failure
clinicalScores.expectedResult: Severe Upper GI Bleed requiring Emergent Endoscopic Intervention
clinicalScores.missingDataBehavior: Must evaluate vitals, hemoglobin, and clinical markers of liver disease.

expectedInvestigations.rationale: Definitive endoscopic diagnosis and endoscopic variceal band ligation (EVL).

expectedInvestigations.testName: Type and Crossmatch 4 Units Packed RBCs
expectedInvestigations.rationale: Maintain hemoglobin between 7 and 8 g/dL.

immediateInterventions: IV Octreotide: 50 mcg IV bolus followed by continuous infusion at 50 mcg/hr for 2-5 days
Prophylactic IV Ceftriaxone 1g IV daily (reduces spontaneous bacterial peritonitis and mortality)
Restrictive blood transfusion strategy: Transfuse PRBCs only to maintain hemoglobin between 7.0 and 8.0 g/dL
Endotracheal intubation prior to endoscopy for airway protection
Emergent EGD within 12 hours for Endoscopic Variceal Ligation (EVL)
definitiveTherapy: Endoscopic band ligation; Transjugular Intrahepatic Portosystemic Shunt (TIPS) if bleeding is refractory

strictContraindications: Liberal blood transfusion targeting Hb > 9-10 g/dL (rebound portal hypertension leads to fatal rebleeding)
Omission of antibiotic prophylaxis (antibiotics prevent bacterial translocation and reduce mortality in cirrhosis GI bleed)
Delaying vasoactive drug infusion until endoscopy is performed
highRiskInteractions: Over-resuscitation with crystalloids and blood dilutes platelets and increases portal venous pressure, dislodging the platelet plug.

criticalFailures.description: Failing to initiate Octreotide and Ceftriaxone immediately or targeting hemoglobin > 9 g/dL in acute variceal bleed

mandatoryActions: IV Octreotide bolus + infusion
IV Ceftriaxone prophylaxis
Restrictive transfusion (Hb 7-8)
Emergent EGD

pastMedicalHistory: Severe alcohol use disorder
Depression

initialPresentation.chiefComplaint: Found unresponsive with deep labored breathing; empty container of automotive antifreeze at side
initialPresentation.onsetAndTimeline: Last seen normal approximately 8 hours ago

releasedFindings: Arterial Blood Gas: pH 7.02, PaCO2 18 mmHg, PaO2 102 mmHg, HCO3 5 mmol/L (life-threatening high anion gap metabolic acidosis).
Basic Metabolic Panel: Sodium 138 mEq/L, Potassium 5.6 mEq/L, Chloride 98 mEq/L, Bicarbonate 5 mEq/L, Creatinine 3.2 mg/dL.
Anion Gap: 138 - (98 + 5) = 35 mEq/L.
Measured Serum Osmolality: 342 mOsm/kg.
Calculated Osmolality: 2*(138) + (90/18) + (14/2.8) = 286 mOsm/kg -> Osmolal Gap = 342 - 286 = 56 mOsm/kg (severely elevated > 10).
progressiveStages.expectedClinicalRealignment: Toxic alcohol poisoning; severe simultaneous high anion gap metabolic acidosis (AG 35) and high osmolal gap (56) in presence of antifreeze ingestion is diagnostic of acute Ethylene Glycol toxicity with glycolate/oxalate nephrotoxicity.

releasedFindings: Urinalysis reveals numerous needle-shaped and envelope-shaped calcium oxalate monohydrate crystals.
Wood's lamp examination of urine exhibits bright green-yellow fluorescence (sodium fluorescein additive in commercial antifreeze).
progressiveStages.expectedClinicalRealignment: CRITICAL ANTIDOTE & DIALYSIS GATING: Immediately administer Fomepizole (15 mg/kg IV loading dose) to block alcohol dehydrogenase and halt production of toxic glycolic/oxalic acid; urgent nephrology consultation for emergent hemodialysis (indicated for pH < 7.25, anion gap > 20, or renal failure).

goldStandard.primaryDiagnosis: Acute Ethylene Glycol Poisoning with Severe Metabolic Acidosis, Acute Kidney Injury, and Oxaluria
goldStandard.clinicalRationale: Massive antifreeze ingestion resulting in severe high anion gap metabolic acidosis (pH 7.02, AG 35), elevated osmolal gap (56 mOsm/kg), acute renal failure (creatinine 3.2), and urine calcium oxalate monohydrate crystals.

clinicalScores.missingDataBehavior: Requires measured freezing point depression osmolality and complete metabolic profile.

expectedInvestigations.testName: Arterial Blood Gas and Basic Metabolic Panel
expectedInvestigations.rationale: Quantify life-threatening acidemia, bicarbonate deficit, and anion gap.

expectedInvestigations.testName: Measured Serum Osmolality and Volatile Screen
expectedInvestigations.rationale: Calculate osmolal gap and exclude ethanol co-ingestion.
Identify pathognomonic calcium oxalate crystals.

immediateInterventions: Immediately administer Fomepizole: 15 mg/kg IV loading dose over 30 minutes (or Ethanol infusion if Fomepizole unavailable)
Emergent Nephrology consultation for urgent hemodialysis to clear parent alcohol and toxic glycolate/oxalate metabolites
IV Sodium Bicarbonate infusion (150 mEq in D5W) to correct severe acidemia (pH < 7.10)
Cofactor therapy: IV Thiamine (100 mg) and Pyridoxine / Vitamin B6 (50 mg) every 6 hours to steer metabolism toward non-toxic alpha-hydroxy-beta-ketoadipate
definitiveTherapy: Emergent hemodialysis until ethylene glycol is undetectable and acidosis has normalized

strictContraindications: Delaying Fomepizole or hemodialysis to await gas chromatography toxic alcohol confirmation (delay results in permanent anuric renal failure or death)
Administering Fomepizole without increasing dose frequency during hemodialysis (Fomepizole is dialyzable; dose every 4 hours during dialysis)
highRiskInteractions: Alcohol dehydrogenase inhibitors only block parent alcohol metabolism; once toxic metabolites have formed and renal failure has ensued, hemodialysis is mandatory.

criticalFailures.description: Failing to initiate Fomepizole/Ethanol or delaying emergent hemodialysis in severe ethylene glycol poisoning

mandatoryActions: Fomepizole 15 mg/kg loading dose
Emergent hemodialysis
Thiamine/Pyridoxine cofactors

initialPresentation.chiefComplaint: Acute presentation of tumor lysis syndrome (tls): Hyperuricemia 14 mg/dL, hyperkalemia 6.4, hyperphosphatemia, acute kidney injury post-chemo
initialPresentation.onsetAndTimeline: Acute onset within recent hours; urgent clinical evaluation required

releasedFindings: Physical examination demonstrates key findings consistent with Tumor Lysis Syndrome (TLS).
Acute diagnostic clues present: Hyperuricemia 14 mg/dL, hyperkalemia 6.4, hyperphosphatemia, acute kidney injury post-chemo.
progressiveStages.expectedClinicalRealignment: Realignment toward high-suspicion of Tumor Lysis Syndrome (TLS).

Critical clinical safety constraint identified.
progressiveStages.expectedClinicalRealignment: Mandatory execution of critical action: Aggressive IV hydration, Rasburicase (0.2 mg/kg IV), continuous ECG telemetry; strict avoidance of Administering IV calcium for hyperphosphatemia-induced hypocalcemia unless tetany/ECG changes.

goldStandard.clinicalRationale: Presentation of Hyperuricemia 14 mg/dL, hyperkalemia 6.4, hyperphosphatemia, acute kidney injury post-chemo in the setting of HEMATOLOGY_ONCOLOGY pathophysiological pathway.

expectedInvestigations.rationale: Rule out mimics and confirm Tumor Lysis Syndrome (TLS).
Anatomical confirmation and risk stratification.

definitiveTherapy: Targeted specialty management for Tumor Lysis Syndrome (TLS)

highRiskInteractions: Failure to adhere to contraindication (Administering IV calcium for hyperphosphatemia-induced hypocalcemia unless tetany/ECG changes) leads to severe clinical deterioration.

mandatoryActions: Aggressive IV hydration, Rasburicase (0.2 mg/kg IV), continuous ECG telemetry
